description-proc.eng: Mechanical Maintenance Services fall under the remit of the University Limerick Campus Technical Services and Sustainability Team, within the Buildings and Estates Department. University Limerick Buildings and Estates Department manage the maintenance and upkeep of the didactic building stock on campus generally through reactive and preventative maintenance tasks and minor works projects should they arise. The services provided by the successful contractors on the framework will typically include; - Planned and reactive maintenance tasks and when required. - Scheduling of planned preventative maintenance activities, based on system specific and legislative requirements. - Management of third-party service providers attending campus for maintenance and minor works tasks, associated with the mechanical systems infrastructure. - Carry out small installations on campus as directed by the Technical Services Engineer. - Engage in quoting for minor works projects. - Out of hours support as required for events, call-outs or necessary emergency works.

This applies particularly to capacity ranges of 100 MW to 500 MW. In this procurement, the Contracting Authority is establishing a framework agreement (hereinafter “Framework Agreement”) with two (2) equipment suppliers of gas pressure reduction and metering skids. The Framework Agreement will be utilized in several upcoming individual projects, primarily related to the natural gas pressure reduction station projects as well as other similar projects of the Contracting Authority. The Scope of Supply includes: • Redundant gas lines from gas feed (filter and heating) to gas outlet (measurement) • Equipment, valves, and piping assembled on one or more skids • The delivery includes design, procurement, manufacturing, inspection, testing, packaging, documentation, and transportation • Design approvals and factory inspections The procurement procedure and the scope of supply has been further described in the Preliminary Technical Scope (Annex 4) (subject to minor changes during the procurement procedure) and in the Annex 1 (Invitation to Participate).

Secondary business objectives relevant to this contract include: Mentorship Support: In addition to the core objectives, the Student Engagement Platform aims to foster a strong mentorship culture by connecting prospective and current students with current Student Ambassadors. Transport is required for Service Users to attend a range of health services including Dialysis, Mental Health, Disability, CADS, Older Persons, Day Care and Acute Services. The scope also includes transport of products (e.g. post, lab samples, medical files, medical products etc). From time to time the Service may also include the provision of transport for members of the public who have been authorised by a Healthcare Facility (i.e. visitors). The Service shall incorporate the provision of both ad-hoc and scheduled journeys via both standard and wheelchair accessible vehicles. Ad-hoc journeys refers to non pre-booked requirements for transportation of Service Users. Scheduled journeys refers to pre-booked transportation requirements and will typically include transport for Renal Dialysis treatments or transport of Service Users for scheduled medical appointments. Both Ad-hoc Runs and Set Runs will be required on a 24-hour 7 day per week basis and will include journeys at weekends, outside business hours and public holidays (i.e. Christmas Day, New Year’s Day, Easter Sunday, etc.) Set Runs are charged on a fixed cost basis and Ad-hoc Runs are charged on a per kilometer basis.

title-proc.eng: Refrigeration system for Isotope Separation System (ISS) of ITER Fuel Cycle

description-proc.eng: ISS is dedicated for separation by means of cryogenic distillation of mixture of hydrogen isotopes intended for ensuring correct composition of ITER fuel mixture. The future tender is for design, procurement, manufacturing, factory testing, delivery, installation, commissioning, and final acceptance of complete refrigeration system, based on Turbo-Brayton reversed refrigeration cycle, intended for delivery of cooling power at 20K level required for operation of cryogenic distillation of ISS.
